text.p: NARODNA OBRODA - Ceskoslovenska Obchodni Banka has taken the Slovak Republic to an international arbitrary court in Washington for failing to repay a 10.7 billion crown debt inherited from the former Czechoslovak Federation.
- Steel maker VSZ posted a pre-tax profit of 543 million crowns in the first half of 1997. The revenues totalled 30 billion crowns.

- Changes in external economic conditions, such as an energy price increase, an import surcharge or the fall of the Czech crown, will boost expenditures of Slovakia's major plastic material producer Chemosvit Svit by some 100 million crowns in the second half of 1997.
- State-owned railway company ZSR posted a loss of 2.68 billion crowns in the first six months of this year, compared with the planned loss of 1.82 billion crowns.
- Slovakia's largest shoe producer Cebo Holding said its sales totalled 1.1 billion crowns for the first half of 1997.
PRAVDA - Finance Ministry said the main reason for the growing state budget deficit was lower-than-expected income tax revenues.
- The Finance Ministry has crititcised the central bank for a "too cautious (monetary) policy which is aimed only at controling of inflation development".

SME - Ludovit Cernak, Deputy-Chairman of the opposition Democratic Union (DU), has accused former economics minister Jan Ducky of being responsible responsible for illegal transfer of 10 percent in chemical company CHZN from an account of the Czech firm Inekon last month.

- The Democratic Coalition, which groups five main opposition parties, has proposed a discussion with parliamentary representatives of all political parties on the possible return of the mandate of Jozef Gaulieder, expelled from the house last December.

HOSPODARSKE NOVINY - Slovakia's sole aluminium producer ZSNP posted a net profit of 212 million crowns in the first half of 1997. The company expects the full year after-tax profit to total some 500 million crowns.
